title: Linear Regression
summary: Predicts Reliance Industries' daily return from the Nifty 50's move and trading volume, using real Yahoo Finance prices.

charts.caption: Reliance and Nifty 50 closing prices from Yahoo Finance, rebased to 100. Reliance has tracked the Nifty 50 with more swing.
Daily Reliance return against the Nifty 50 return. Red circles are stock-specific outliers that were kept; orange crosses are crash and election-day moves outside the form's range.
Predicted against actual daily returns on the most recent 25% of days.
Residuals show no trend against the prediction, but a few days are missed by 4 to 8 points.
Learned coefficients: the market coefficient is the stock's beta; volume adds a small positive effect.
Residuals are centred near zero with heavy tails: occasional stock-specific days the model cannot see.

title: Decision Tree
summary: Decides whether a loan application is approved using a short tree of yes/no questions you can read.

charts.caption: The learned tree (top two levels): each box is a yes/no question about the applicant.
Which questions the tree relies on most when deciding.
Deeper trees memorise the training data; held-out accuracy stops improving early.
Confusion matrix on held-out data.

title: Random Forest
summary: Forecasts Reliance Industries' next-month volatility from recent volatility, India VIX and price action, using real Yahoo Finance data.

charts.caption: Reliance's 20-day range-based volatility next to India VIX. The spikes are real (March 2020, the 2024 election result, single-day shocks); red circles mark stock-specific outlier days, which were kept.
The forest's forecast against what happened over the next 20 days, on the most recent days held out from training. It tracks the broad level but cannot foresee sudden shocks.
Predicted against actual 20-day volatility on the test period. Forecasts are compressed towards the middle: the extremes are not predicted.
Test-period error for five forecasts. Simply carrying today's volatility forward is a hard baseline to beat; the forest and a straight line both do a little better.
Which inputs the forest relies on, measured by how much accuracy falls when each is scrambled. The 60-day level anchors the forecast; bars below zero are inputs that add noise on the test period.

Predicted volatility as the last 20 days get more volatile, other inputs held at typical values. Both models stay close to the 60-day level instead of carrying a spike forward, which is why simply repeating the last 20 days does worse.
